transcript: Did you know that if you press your tongue firmly against the roof of your mouth and at the same time massage the spot between your eyebrows for about 15 seconds, your stuffy nose will clear in under a minute. This pressure activates your sinuses and disrupts the swelling signals so you can breathe freely again. Most people reach for nasal sprays and decongestants without knowing that everything they need is already built into their own body. Your sinuses are controlled by pressure points that have been mapped for thousands of years. When you press the tongue against the roof of the mouth, you create an internal pressure that pushes against the vomer bone. This bone runs through the center of your nasal passages when it rocks gently back and forth. The congestion begins to loosen. At the same time, the point between the eyebrows connects directly to the nerves that control sinus drainage. When you stimulate both at once, you are giving your body a command to open. It is not a trick. It is anatomy. The elder monks taught me this when I was young. In our monastery, we have never needed medicine for a blocked nose. But here is what most people do not realize. A blocked nose is not always about a cold. Stress tightens the muscles around your sinuses. Tension restricts blood flow to the face. Shallow breathing from anxiety keeps everything congested. Many people walk around with a stuffy nose for weeks and blame the weather or allergies when the real cause is a nervous system that will not relax. When your body is tense, everything tightens, including the passages you breathe through. Save this video for when you need it. Write in the comments. Breathe if this helped you. And if you want to learn how to calm the tension that keeps your body tight, how to release what blocks not just your nose but your sleep, your energy, your peace. I spent over 20 years learning in silence how to do exactly that. And everything I know is inside the way back to stillness. The link is in my profile.
